notes: Measured by `grit-bench daily` on unmodified main af5742af4e81372f72ef1710a31e9c032e43c1f6 (cargo release profile, system git 2.43.0, no baseline grit release; no source changes, nothing landed on main). Task day is 2026-10-31 (dispatched 23:01 UTC); the published measurements were taken 2026-11-01T00:09:57Z to about 01:56Z (the timestamp field is the start of the measured pass; the `date` field keeps the task day). A first single-invocation full pass (started 23:11 UTC) aborted after ~35 min at fetch/incremental@git-git because grit-bench stops the whole run on any failed correctness check and writes no partial output, so it was discarded. The published pass ran every one of the 171 daily scenarios as its own `grit-bench daily --only <id>` invocation (defaults: 3 warmups, adaptive 5-20 samples) so that failures stay in the report; headline rows first. Published fields rename median_wall_ms to median_ms and convert peak_rss_bytes to max_rss_kb (bytes/1024); each scenario's detail object (setup, prepare, commands, correctness, phases) is carried unchanged from the runner's first pass. Functional areas are mapped to the public schema (blame/revwalk->history, bundles/notes/odb/packs->objects, config/hooks->other, diff/ignore/index/worktrees->worktree, remotes->remote). Headline flags/names come from the runner's registry, which also flags branch/list-json, branch/merged, log/json-100, pull/rebase and push/force-with-lease as headline in addition to the 17 required ones. Repo metadata (files, commits, refs, pack_mb) is carried over from the 2026-10-27 report; the fixtures are deterministic and pinned (git.git v2.47.0), and files/commits/refs were re-counted for git-git, synth-10k, small, many-refs and many-refs-loose and match. grit-http-server was built (cargo build --release -p grit-http-server) and put on PATH after the first pass; the four HTTP scenarios (clone/http, clone/shallow-depth1-http, fetch/incremental-http, push/incremental-http) were then run, so they are measured. Noise check against the previous report (2026-10-27; same machine type and git 2.43.0): 21 scenarios had a grit/git time ratio >20% worse or a peak-memory ratio >30% worse and were re-run three more times each with `daily --only <id>`; the published median/stddev use all concatenated samples, runs is their count, min/max span all invocations, max_rss_kb is the maximum observed, and detail is from the first pass: add/all-ignorecase@synth-100k, add/all@synth-100k, add/modified@big-blobs, clone/bare@synth-10k, clone/blobless@git-git, clone/full@git-git, clone/http@synth-10k, clone/local@synth-10k, diff/stat@synth-100k, diff/worktree@big-blobs, fetch/dry-run@git-git, fetch/incremental-http@git-git, gc/default@synth-10k, rebase/onto@git-git, reflog/list@synth-10k, repack/full@git-git, reset/hard-delete-heavy@wide-48k, reset/sparse@sparse-120k, reset/sparse@sparse-240k, rm/dry-run@synth-10k, status/dirty@synth-100k. Failures: 7 (fetch/deepen@git-git, fetch/incremental@git-git, fetch/one-branch@git-git, pull/check@git-git, pull/fast-forward@git-git, pull/rebase@synth-10k, reset/blobless@git-git). For these the runner aborts the scenario before publishing any timing, so both git and grit are null, error holds the runner's message, and commands/prepare/correctness are copied from the previous report. The failures are: grit fetch/pull over a file:// remote of git.git fails with `refusing to point ref 'refs/remotes/origin/master' at <oid>: no such object in the repository` (fetch/incremental, fetch/one-branch, pull/fast-forward; the same fetch over smart HTTP, fetch/incremental-http, works), fetch/deepen fails with `unexpected EOF after done`, pull/check and pull/rebase fail in the timed grit run (exit 1), and reset/blobless fails its correctness check (`blobless materialization produced 4 packs`). Because two headline rows (fetch, pull) have no git or grit numbers today, they could not be compared. No scenarios were skipped.
